cues.text: "Dangerously Yours"
"Dangerously Yours"
A half hour of romance and adventure
brought to you at this time each Sunday by the Vick Chemical Company
and today bringing you a special short version of “Masquerade”
an exciting tale of espionage in the Budapest of 1915.
I am adventure.
In my name men have traversed the highways, the byways, the skyways of the world.
I have tramped the jungles with explorers.
I have ridden the wilderness road on horseback and in covered wagons.
I have gone 20,000 leagues under the seas and as many leagues above them.
I have been the fire of Captain Kidd and Walter Raleigh and John Paul Jones and
François Villon.
That fire that burns in the heart of youth, that makes men dream and dare and
conquer.
I am the spirit of romantic adventure.
I am dangerously yours.
Today follow me to a dark room in the Europe of 25 years ago
where a woman sits looking across a desk into eyes that are focused on history.
Masquerade!
And so, my Countess Rachola, you have a reason for choosing you for this mission.
You are very young, you are clever, and you are very beautiful.
Because of your youth you should be exceptionally valuable to us.
I am at your command, Excellency.
Now, you'll forget my title.
In all our communications you will address me as Mr. Kolenkov.
Now, let us get on to facts.
I hope the Count will not be too difficult for you as a should man.
When you have obtained the information you will conceal the message in this silver
pencil.
Send it to me immediately. Trust no one.
We rely on your discretion.
I understand.
Well, now in these papers you will find all the necessary information about cow
bestifan.
It has already been arranged just how you will meet him.
Tonight you will take the train to Budapest.
Good evening, madam.
I have my bag sent to suite 913.
Yes, ma'am.
Good evening, Countess Rachola.
Good evening.
Welcome back, Countess Rachola.
Thank you for today.
Our table's for one, madam. Is Count Estefan dining?
Oh, he's at the table by the window, madam.
I can't imagine whatever possessed queer there said.
I drove fencing my prices five hours ago.
This morning when I was riding in the park I saw Duffy on the bridle track.
I beg your pardon, madam.
Here is the necklace and the rings and the brace that you gave me, Luigi.
Take them back. I'm through.
Just a moment, madam. You've made a... madam, wait!
Can I be of service, Count Estefan?
Did you see the young lady who stopped at my table?
Yes.
She left these jewels. I don't understand.
Do you know who she is?
She is the Countess Rachola.
She's in suite 913.
Just a moment.
Madam, you have made a mistake.
My name is not Luigi.
I have never seen you or these jewels before.
I know. Won't you come in, Count Estefan?
You... you know who I am?
But of course, you were the most handsome man in the dining room.
And I was very lonely.
So I thought tonight I will have an adventure.
I will make the acquaintance of the distinguished Count Estefan.
How do you know my name?
It was not difficult to find out.
How did you know I wouldn't run off with your jewels?
I took that chance, besides they're insured.
Are you angry?
No, I am not angry.
If some kind fate wishes to send a beautiful lady to dine with me,
I can only be grateful.
You will do me the honor, won't you, madam?
I shall be delighted.
What would you like for dinner?
What does a Count eat?
Peasants' wings and peacocks' breasts and...
What do you usually eat?
What does a Countess usually eat?
Almost anything.
Well then, how about roast beef?
All right.
Step right up, face your gun,
and watch Mademoiselle in the red hat
shoot the little clay pigeon.
Step right up.
I'll never be able to hear a thing.
Don't let me down before all these people.
I'll try.
Hand the little lady down a dancing dog.
Step right up.
Look, Catherine, a shooting star.
Did you wish?
I didn't have time.
Then there is something you wish for.
Yes.
What did you wish?
I was wishing that we were two other people,
two people who need not say goodbye.
Perhaps it can be that way.
[music]
Forgive me, Your Lordship,
but I'm not easy in my mind about this business.
I wish you wouldn't go to see that woman tonight, sir.
How could I stay away?
Headbare, for the first time in my life,
I am completely head over heels in love.
But, Countess, if I'm not...
I know what you're thinking.
I have a mission to perform,
and I have no right to fall in love.
But things don't always work out the way
we'd like to have them work out, Headbare.
Oh, I don't know what's to come of all this, sir.
No, Headbare, neither do I.
Neither do I.
But perhaps we shall find out tonight.
[music]
Catherine, I have received a message for you from Mr. Kolenkov.
What is it?
He said that you must obtain our information immediately.
That you've taken too long.
You're to get it tonight.
Tonight?
Mr. Kolenkov has been lenient with you
because this is your first mission.
But he will not be lenient any longer.
It is not wise to anger Mr. Kolenkov.
He is a dangerous enemy.
Forgive me, Catherine, I was sent to serve you as a maid,
not to give you advice.
You're right.
Don't worry.
The mission will be completed tonight.
You have the silver pencil.
Yes.
Then I will wait for you at the appointed place.
Do not fail us.
The mission will be completed tonight.
[music]
Catherine, I offer you the three things most dear to me.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: My heart, my country, and my dream.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: You are too generous.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: Catherine, you must listen to me.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Since that first hour we met, I've been completely yours.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: There's never been anyone else for me.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: There never will.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Oh, please, please don't say anymore.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: There are worlds between us, worlds that can't be bridged with words.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: You said one night that you wished we were two different people.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: I think you may have that wish, Catherine.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: What do you mean?
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: Only that my country is close to its victory
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: and may not need so much of my service any longer.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Close to victory?
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: I'm going to tell you something tonight, Catherine.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Something that will put my life in your hands.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Your life?
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: It would mean my life for the news to get to certain circles.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Then don't tell me.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: How do you know you can trust me?
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: I love you, and I believe you love me.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: You're quite wrong.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: This has been only an adventure to me.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: That isn't true, Catherine.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: It is true.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: You smiled at me.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: I was flattered.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: It was an adventure for a holiday mood.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: You may as well take my heart, Catherine.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: It's already full of you.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: You walked into it the day we met.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: [Unclear]
But isn't any man who falls in love?
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Do you know what you are to me?
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: You're something to believe in again.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: You're a type of person that had ceased to exist for me.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: A fine and honest woman.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Oh, my darling, you're such a child.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: Take your foolish little dream in your heart and go.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: Please go.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: What is it?
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: What's wrong, my dear?
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: You know nothing about me.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: You've known me only three weeks.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: Three weeks?
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Catherine, I've known you all my life.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: All your life.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: It's true.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: I've seen you in a thousand plays, read you in as many books.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: When I've heard beautiful music, I've thought she'd like that.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: I've looked at flowers and known that one day I give them to you.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Oh, stop, stop.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: You must listen to me.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: I'm not that woman.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: Perhaps I was once, but I'm not now.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: You see, you were wrong.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: You can't trust me.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: Are you trying to tell me that someone whose name we both know
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: and won't mention sent you?
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: What are you saying?
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: You see, I've known all along.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: I had her bear look you up the day you arrived.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: And it didn't make any difference?
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: It didn't make any difference.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: You see, I trust you.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: You came here to betray me and to betray my country.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: That is your mission, Countess Rachola.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: And yet I am so sure of your love that I will trust you with my life
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: and what is far more valuable, the life of my country.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: I will betray you.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: If you do, you will betray yourself at the same time.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Yes. Yes, I know.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: So you shall know my secret.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Even now, as we sit here, there is a great network
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: growing tighter around the foremost nations of the world.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Treaties, pacts, alliances being formed against the man who sent you.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Tonight, I will sign a pact that will set the wheels in motion to destroy him.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Destroy him? No.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: He's made a great many mistakes.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: The greatest of all was sending you here, Catherine.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: Why?
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: He knew I should love you.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: But he did not guess that you would fall in love with me.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: No. He didn't guess that.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: Then you do see that you cannot betray him.
cues.speaker: Estefan

cues.text: If I betray you, I betray myself.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text: If I betray him, I betray my country.
cues.speaker: Catherine

cues.text:
My country is very dear to me.
— Dearer than I?
No. No, not dearer than you.
Then will you help me defeat him?
Help you defeat him?
By telling me his plans. That's the only way I can hope to defeat him.
We can't both win. You'll see, Catherine.
I'm beginning to see. And you will help me?
By giving you any information I may possess concerning our plans?
Yes.
You're very clever, aren't you?
Oh, I can read you like a book now.
You thought I was young and easily swayed.
That you could make me love you. And I would throw over my country, my duty for you.
That's not the way to look at it, Catherine.
You weren't so wise after all. Because you've lost, you hear me? Lost.
You guessed wrong in our little duel of wits.
You forgot how close hate is to love.
You don't know what you're saying, Catherine.
You never loved me. You knew that I loved you. And you used that.
Catherine, stop talking like a child. We're playing for countries now.
Yes, we are, aren't we?
This is a gun in my hand, Rudolph.
I'd advise you to be careful what you say.
Well, rather melodramatic, aren't you?
Tell me, will I be the seventh notch on the gun or the eighth?
Do you mind if I smoke?
Smoke?
I always smoke at the theatre.
Somehow it enhances the performance.
You can do anything you please, Rudolph.
But you have very little time to do it in.
You mean you're actually going to kill me?
I mean just that.
Well, go ahead.
I'll do this my own way.
Look, you already know my purpose in being here.
Now, you will either give me my information or I will kill you.
You have until nine o'clock.
You won't do it.
You can't pull the trigger.
You can't pull it because you love me.
It takes a very brave and a very cold woman to do that, Catherine.
I don't think you can.
Isn't that true?
Isn't that why you're waiting?
That's not true.
Or is it that you want to watch your victim?
You want my heart to constrict with agony my hands to shake.
You want me to plead for my life so you can make a generous gesture and spare me.
Sorry, Catherine, I don't seem to be in the mood for prayers tonight.
You don't think I'll do it.
That's why you're so brave.
You don't think I'll do it.
You wouldn't be so brave otherwise.
You're a coward at heart.
You lied to me.
You deceived me.
You try to deceive me.
I'm tired of listening to you.
You gave me your heart, you know.
You'd like me to hand it back whole again, but I won't.
You live a long time yet, Catherine, in eternity without me.
You will look into the faces of passers-by hoping for something that will, for an
instant, bring me back to you.
You will find moonlit nights strangely empty because when you call my name through
them, there will be no answer.
Always your heart will be aching for me, and your mind will give you the doubtful
consolation that you did a brave thing.
You dare to talk of bravery?
What else do we have to talk about, Catherine?
For me, there will never be another woman but you.
But for my heart, there is another love that must come before you, my country.
You're so still. Your face is like ice.
What are you thinking, Catherine?
What does anything you can say matter?
You betrayed me with words.
What good are words when your heart is breaking?
If I fail now, I should deserve to die.
You tricked me into loving you.
Aren't you forgetting that you came here for the same purpose?
I couldn't have betrayed you. I tried to tell you.
You said you already knew. I was as honest as I knew how to be.
Do you think I wanted to love you, knowing where you came from and what your
mission was?
Don't you suppose that every hour we were together, I was thinking she's just
pretending?
You wasn't. I loved you.
And I loved you so much, I let you pretend.
Because you brought something to my days, I couldn't stand the thought of losing.
Listen to your heart, Catherine. Feel it pounding.
Your time is up.
Then my last words. I love you, Catherine.
You're determined to die with a lie on your lips.
I love you, Catherine.
Oh, God.
I'll bear. I'll bear.
Where are you, sir? I heard a shot.
Help me up. I'll be all right. Help me up.
Oh, I knew you should never have come here. I'll get a doctor.
No, no, no, no. No, it's too late.
I waited right by the door like you told me to, sir.
The other woman went downstairs about ten minutes ago.
Please let me get a doctor, sir.
No, no. I want you to send a message, though, at once.
The usual destination. Yes, sir.
Kolenkov, the masquerade is over. X-32 reports that Countess Rachola is trustworthy and loyal.
You may entrust in her care any documents.
She will not betray you.
Report case 255, closed.
X-32. Conceal it as usual. I'll bear in the silver pencil.
Please let me call her back.
You must tell her the truth before it's too late.
Tell her the truth.
Tell her the truth so that she will watch the stars through tears
instead of following the one cold star that is her destiny.
No, no, I'll bear. Let her think I never loved her.
One day she will follow a flag to the same fate as mine.
We must leave her the strength for that hour.
I am adventure.
Today you have shared the adventure of masquerade with me.
Next week I bring you Jungle Harvest, take you to the tropic paradise of Samburam,
to share the adventure of a gentle, peace-loving man,
suddenly forced to pit his wits against the sinister and the dangerous,
in order to save his own life and the life of the girl he loves.
Until then, I am dangerously yours.
